label: early original-phase input p (or k after n/1/f/p/z/k/b/s)
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (99% of mass), firing at t=1..5 (peak t=2-3) and never at t=0 or t>=6. Driven mainly by the current input: p (16x lift, 64% of mass) and k (7x, 19%), with weaker firing on 1, u, n, q, f. Magnitude is modulated by the preceding context: strongest when the earlier inputs are from {n,1,f,p,z,k,b,s} (top examples are n n [p], n f [p], n 1 [p]); p after other letters (e.g. late in the sequence or after y/d/w) is often inactive. Hardly fires at <DEL> or in the copy phase. The predicate gets most of the mass but precision is about 0.5 because the context dependence looks graded rather than a clean token set.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (input phase: p, k, 1, u; copy phase: p, k, q, u; delimiter step: ) and the previous input (most: n, f, 1, p, z, k; least: t, i, 3, c); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, L=3 & t=5, t=2.
